title: complexity depth --json
description: The interface depth signal for the shallow module and pass-through red flags: exported functions, classes and modules, and the exported pass-throughs, the removable ones first, then the ones an interface or a framework requires. A whole-repository run on a clean tree is also stored as the complexity.depth report.

shallow.description: Nodes per interface element below which an exported unit is shallow.

includeTests.description: True when --include-tests listed the test rows with the production ones.

filesWithoutAdapter.description: Text files in the selection that cannot be measured for depth.

passThroughByKind.description: The listed pass-throughs by what keeps them: removable (nothing outside fixes them), interface (they implement or override an inherited method) and entryPoint (a framework calls them by an attribute).

passThroughNotExported.description: Pass-through functions that have no row because their language does not export them (private, internal, package-private, lower-case or underscore-prefixed, or in a type that is not exported). Counted whatever their role.

unit.description: The qualified name, or the path for a module.

id.description: path#Qualified.name, or the path for a module.

exported.description: Exported by its file (public, capitalised, `export` or `pub`, by language), or a public method of an exported class.

interface.description: Interface size: parameters, or constructor parameters plus reachable members, or exported names.

depth.description: nodes divided by interface, to two places.

passThrough.description: The call the function's whole body forwards to.

required.description: What fixes the unit's name and signature, where the language shows it: interface for a method that implements or overrides an inherited one (Rust trait impl, @Override, override), entry-point for a function a framework calls by an attribute (Rust procedural macro). Null otherwise.

score.description: The reciprocal of depth. Rows are ordered by group (pass-throughs that are not required, then required pass-throughs, then the rest), then by score, highest first, then by path.
